paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God wants to live with His people. He says, "And they are to make a sanctuary for Me, so that I may dwell among them." (Exodus 25:8) Every piece of gold, every pole and every lamp in this passage points back to that one wish. He wasn't building a fancy room for Himself but making a way to be close.

Now look at how He asks: the offering comes from "every man whose heart compels him." (Exodus 25:2) Nobody got squeezed and nobody got guilted. Then God tells Moses to make everything "according to the pattern I show you" (Exodus 25:9), so the design belonged to Him and the giving belonged to them. That's the deal, baker: God sets the pattern, and you bring a willing heart, and trust me, a stamper who got called out of a junk drawer knows a willing heart is plenty to bring.

And the closeness is the point. God says, "I will meet with you there above the mercy seat… I will speak with you…" (Exodus 25:22) Bread sits before Him "at all times" (Exodus 25:30), and lamps light the area in front of the lampstand. So when you open the Word today, come ready to listen, friend, because He's still speaking and still wanting to be near.
